summary: Open platform in a Mount Hood NF ponderosa pine, dated to about 1930, with a 1940s cabin; a 2021 visit found remnants and the FFLA list marks the site abandoned.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says the platform sat atop a 70 ft tree; a 1934 entry on the Forest Lookouts county page says a 100-foot tree. Both are reported in the story; no height is used as a fact.

Firelookout.com says the platform is apparently still there; a 2021 visitor found the cabin gone but pieces of platform and ladder still visible; the FFLA Oregon list says Abandoned. The story gives the two accounts and uses abandoned, the FFLA label. The 1979 inventory is not used for Joe's Point: on the Forest Lookouts page it belongs to PEBBLE POINT TREE.

The register gives N 45.427267, W 121.420554; the record and the FFLA index give 45.4284, -121.41436, about half a kilometre apart. Not resolved; the record's values were kept because they match the FFLA index.

sources.title: Crow's Nests of Mt Hood National Forest

notes_for_editor: The register URL path says /wa/ and the registry number says WA 440, but the site is in Wasco County, Oregon, so the record's OR state is right. The brief's conflict list says ffla=gone, but the FFLA Oregon index row reads Abandoned; a status correction is proposed. The 1936 telephone ring and the December 1979 inventory were removed from this record: the cached Forest Lookouts page places both under PEBBLE POINT TREE, not JOES POINT TREE. The 1935 ring and the June 1934 100-foot crow's nest stay, since they sit inside the JOES POINT TREE block. No photo with a usable image URL was found; the register's 1959 Dennis Lynch photo and the Fire Lookout Museum photo have no URL in the pages read. Fate rests on one undated firelookout.com note and one 2021 personal blog visit, plus the FFLA Abandoned label. The blog gives parking and hiking directions; the story summarises them. No current access rules were found.
